programme.desc: «Plus+ Report. Maestro Obradovic» Nine-time European champion with five different teams. His passion, intensity and vehemence have marked European basketball for more than thirty years. Zeljko Obradovic was a world champion as a player with a legendary Yugoslav team before making an early move to the bench. It was in 1991, with Partizan Belgrade, the team of his life. His first season he was already European champion. Joventut, Real Madrid, Treviso, Panathinaikos and Fenerbahçe later saw him triumph. Along the way he has marked the lives and careers of hundreds of players. Many call him teacher. Obradovic returned home, to Partizan, where they adore him. And he closed the circle with his resignation in November 2025. In any case, he remains one of the main references of European basketball of all time

programme.desc: 2020 г. Год: 2020. Страна: JAV, Kanada. Год: 2020. S1, Ep3 «America's Wild Seasons»…In autumn, change sweeps across America. As the trees greet the chill with a blaze of color, it's make or break time for animals. Time to pull up stakes, make last minute preparations, and often find a mate before the cold sets inThe wilds of America are vast and untamed. Over the course of a year, this immersive documentary series investigates the perils and challenges faced by the animals that inhabit these ferocious wildernesses. Through winter, spring, summer and autumn witness how the ever changing conditions affect life on land, below the waves and in the air. The personalities and characters of certain animals will develop as the series progress and you will find yourself rooting for your favourites to survive as the seasons go by. America's seasons are wild and extreme posing many trails to the varied wildlife that live there. From freezing rains to scorching deserts, the weather is as scary and unpredictable as it could possibly be. Nature documentary seriesDirector: Jeff MoralesCast: Scott McNeil

programme.title: Terra X
programme.desc: The deep sea is by far the largest habitat on our planet. 62 percent of the earth's surface lies in a water depth of over 1000 meters. Not a ray of sunshine penetrates this barely explored world, and yet absolute darkness does not reign here. It has long been known that deep sea creatures such as frogfish and squid have light organs. But scientists recently discovered that almost all organisms in this zone emit light signals, but they are so weak that humans do not notice them - unlike ghost fish, for example, whose huge eyes are hidden under a transparent skull cap. Highly sensitive cameras make the mysterious lights visible for the first time.
